# 1 Samuel Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 133v–134r | **Source Image:** 1SA_004_page_001.jpg, 1SA_004_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle. They encamped beside Ebenezer, and the Philistines encamped at Aphek.

**2** The Philistines drew up in battle array against Israel, and as the battle spread, Israel was struck down before the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men on the field of battle.

**3** When the troops returned to camp, the elders of Israel said, "Why has the LORD struck us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, that it may come into our midst and save us from the hand of our enemies."

**4** So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned upon the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

**5** When the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel raised such a great shout that the earth resounded.

**6** The Philistines heard the sound of the shout and said, "What is this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they learned that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.

**7** And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, "A god has come into the camp." And they said, "Woe to us! Nothing like this has happened before.

**8** Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every kind of plague in the wilderness.

**9** Take courage and be men, O Philistines, lest you become servants to the Hebrews as they have served you. Be men and fight!"

**10** So the Philistines fought, and Israel was struck down, and every man fled to his tent. The slaughter was very great — thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.

**11** The ark of God was captured, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

**12** A man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh that same day, with his garments torn and earth upon his head.

**13** When he arrived, there was Eli, sitting on his seat by the side of the road, watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came to report in the city, the whole city cried out.

**14** Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said, "What is this sound of tumult?" And the man hurried and came and reported to Eli.

**15** Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were set so that he could not see.

**16** The man said to Eli, "I am the one who has come from the battle line — I fled from the front lines today." And Eli said, "What happened, my son?"

**17** The messenger answered, "Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been captured."

**18** The moment he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backward from his seat beside the gate, and his neck broke, and he died — for the man was old and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.

**19** Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard that the ark of God was captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she collapsed and gave birth, for her labor pains seized her.

**20** As she lay dying, the women attending her said, "Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son." But she did not answer, nor did she take it to heart.

**21** She named the child Ichabod, saying, "The glory has departed from Israel" — because of the capture of the ark of God, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.

**22** She said, "The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Strong agreement across all three translators on narrative structure and verse count (22). The fourfold escalation of bad news in v. 17 and the theological priority of the ark over human deaths (vv. 18-22) were consistently recognized.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### Verse 2 — "struck down" vs. "defeated" vs. "crushed"
- **EMET:** "was struck Israel before the Philistines"
- **LOGOS:** "Israel was struck down before the Philistines"
- **PNEUMA:** "Israel was defeated"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS with "struck down" — preserving the Hebrew nikkah while being readable.

### Verse 3 — "Let us bring/take" and "save us"
- **EMET:** "Let us take to ourselves... let it save us"
- **LOGOS:** "Let us bring to ourselves... that it may come into our midst and save us"
- **PNEUMA:** "Let's bring the ark... If it goes with us into battle, it will save us"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS. PNEUMA's addition "If it goes with us into battle" is interpretive.

### Verse 5 — "shout"
- **EMET:** "shouted all Israel a great shout, and resounded the earth"
- **LOGOS:** "all Israel raised a great shout, and the earth resounded"
- **PNEUMA:** "all Israel let out such a thunderous shout that the ground shook"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS. PNEUMA's "thunderous" and "ground shook" are vivid but add interpretation.

### Verse 7 — "God" vs. "A god"
- **EMET:** "God has come to the camp"
- **LOGOS:** "God has come into the camp"
- **PNEUMA:** "A god has come into their camp"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows PNEUMA with "A god" — from the Philistine polytheistic perspective, this is more contextually accurate.

### Verse 10 — "fled to his tent" vs. "fled to his home"
- **EMET:** "fled each man to his tent"
- **LOGOS:** "every man fled to his tent"
- **PNEUMA:** "Every man fled to his home"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS with "tent" (Hebrew ohel) — the literal term.

### Verse 18 — "when he mentioned" vs. "the moment"
- **EMET:** "as he mentioned"
- **LOGOS:** "when he mentioned"
- **PNEUMA:** "The moment he mentioned"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts PNEUMA's "the moment" — it captures the dramatic immediacy of the Hebrew temporal clause.

### Verse 19 — "bowed down" / "knelt" / "collapsed"
- **EMET:** "she knelt and gave birth"
- **LOGOS:** "she bowed down and gave birth"
- **PNEUMA:** "she collapsed and went into labor"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA uses "collapsed" — the Hebrew kara' means to bow/sink down, and in this context of sudden shock, "collapsed" captures the physical reality.

— SOPHIA
